item.title: Elbows and Chin Up: A Whirlwind Week in the U.S.-Canada Trade War
item.description: After trade talks collapsed, Mark Carney rallied the nation, Canadian businesses stood defiant, and President Trump moved to rename Lake Ontario.
item.dc:creator: Matina Stevis-Gridneff, Ian Austen and Vjosa Isai
item.media:credit: Dave Chan; Jim Watson/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: President Trump and Prime Minister Mark Carney are at odds again.

item.title: Carney Has Canadians’ Support on Trump. Now Comes the Hard Part.
item.description: The U.S.-Canada trade war has galvanized Canadians behind their prime minister’s decision to walk away from negotiations. What happens when the time comes for talks to restart?
item.dc:creator: Matina Stevis-Gridneff
item.media:description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney speaks at a news conference in Ottawa, Ontario, after trade talks with the US collapsed earlier this month.

item.title: Chevron Is in Talks to Expand in Venezuela, a Potential Win for Trump
item.description: President Trump’s administration has been pushing U.S. companies like Chevron to invest more in Venezuela’s oil industry.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca F. Elliott, Simon Romero, Anatoly Kurmanaev and Lisa Friedman
item.media:description: A Chevron-chartered oil tanker was anchored near Maracaibo, Venezuela, in February. Chevron is the only U.S. oil company with a major footprint in the country.

item.title: A Venezuelan Colonel Turned Actor Is Deported From Florida
item.description: A former lieutenant colonel in Venezuela’s National Guard living in Florida was deported, interrupting a lawsuit that accused him of ordering violent raids and torture.
item.dc:creator: Zane Irwin and Frances Robles
item.category: Human Rights and Human Rights Violations

item.title: Fire Outside Home of Canadian Parliament Member Is Under Investigation
item.description: Two cars were destroyed at the Toronto home of Salma Zahid, a Liberal member of Parliament, in an overnight episode condemned by Prime Minister Mark Carney.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra E. Petri
item.media:credit: Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press, via Associated Press
item.media:description: Salma Zahid, who represents the Scarborough Centre-Don Valley East federal electoral district in the province of Ontario, said though vehicles were destroyed, she and her family were safe.

item.title: Canada Hires U.S. Scholars From Harvard and Other Top Universities
item.description: A crackdown on American academia by the Trump administration has handed Canadian universities a rare opportunity to lure some top researchers north.
item.dc:creator: Vjosa Isai
item.media:credit: Nasuna Stuart-Ulin for The New York Times
item.media:description: McGill University in Montreal is one of the schools that has benefited from the Canada-bound brain drain from U.S. institutions.

item.title: Yielding on French Could Restart Trade Talks, Canadian Officials Say
item.description: Canada’s minister in charge of trade with the U.S. was responding to comments by Jamieson Greer, the U.S. trade representative. But that was before any mention of Lake Ontario.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen and Vjosa Isai
item.media:description: Dominic LeBlanc, Canada’s minister responsible for trade with the United States, center, with Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada.

item.title: Trump Administration to Expand Deportation Flights to Haiti
item.description: Flights to the Caribbean nation will increase from once a month to once a week now that the Supreme Court allowed President Trump to cancel a humanitarian program.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Aleaziz, Zolan Kanno-Youngs and Frances Robles
item.media:description: Deportation flights to Haiti will increase as soon as this week.

item.title: Man Is Arrested in Fatal Shooting of Mexican Influencer During Livestream
item.description: The authorities accused the man of attacking César Gastélum, a young influencer, during a livestream in Sinaloa this month.
item.dc:creator: Ali Watkins
item.media:description: A memorial near the restaurant in Culiacán, Mexico, where César Gastélum was shot dead this month.

item.title: As Anger Grows Over Trump Tariffs, Some in Canada Want Out of U.S. F-35 Deal
item.description: A year into a government review of the purchase of as many as 88 F-35s, one premier says buying American warplanes makes no sense in the face of President Trump’s latest tariffs.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:description: The F-35 Lightning, made by American defense contractor Lockheed-Martin, costs between $82.5 million and $109 million per plane, depending on the variant.

item.title: Democratic Socialists Are the Toast of the Party in Uruguay
item.description: The success of progressive candidates in the United States is inspiring leftists abroad struggling under pressure from the Trump administration and its allies.
item.dc:creator: Jack Nicas and Anita Pouchard Serra
item.media:credit: Anita Pouchard Serra for The New York Times
item.media:description: Participants at the Panamerican Congress in Montevideo, Uruguay.

item.title: Russian Sanctions Are Fueling a Canadian Car Theft Epidemic
item.description: Russia is the largest destination for stolen Canadian cars. Smugglers are meeting the demand of a booming black market.
item.dc:creator: Jane Bradley and Michael Schwirtz

item.title: After Whiskey With His Captors, Cuban Dissident Lands in a Miami Maelstrom
item.description: The former political prisoner Luis Manuel Otero Alcántara is unpacking 4,000 paintings he brought to Miami from Cuba and dodging criticism from exiles who once welcomed him.
item.dc:creator: Frances Robles and David C. Adams
item.media:credit: Martina Tuaty for The New York Times
item.media:description: Luis Manuel Otero Alcántara with one of his sculptures last month in Miami.

item.title: Wasps Sting Climber More Than 100 Times Before She Is Rescued by Helicopter
item.description: A 33-year-old woman was rescued along with her climbing partner on Tuesday after she was stung while hiking in the British Columbia backcountry north of Vancouver.
item.dc:creator: Alena Cerro
item.media:description: Lions Bay Search and Rescue responded with a helicopter to rescue a hiker who had been badly stung by wasps in the backcountry north of Vancouver, British Columbia, on Tuesday.

item.title: A Movement to Restrict Social Media for Children Has Taken Hold Globally
item.description: Governments around the world have passed or proposed a range of bans or restrictions on young teens using addictive social media platforms.
item.dc:creator: Ephrat Livni
item.media:description: A 15-year-old using social media apps in Australia in July, more than half a year after the country had implemented a ban on children under 16 using many platforms.

item.title: Canadians Stand Their Ground Amid New Trump Tariffs and Expanding U.S.-Canada Trade War
item.description: Business owners are preparing for financial pain after the latest U.S.-Canada trade talks collapsed. But many Canadians are embracing a show of resistance.

item.media:credit: Nick Iwanyshyn/The Canadian Press, via Associated Press
item.media:description: Of Canadian politicians’ responses to the trade war, perhaps the most colorful came from Doug Ford, the premier of Ontario, on Monday.

item.title: Worker Dies After Accident With Plane at Montreal Airport
item.description: The Transportation Safety Board of Canada said the episode involved an Airbus A350 operated by French Bee, a French low-cost airline.
item.dc:creator: Johnny Diaz
item.media:description: The authority that operates Montréal-Trudeau International Airport said a worker employed by Samsic, a company that provides support services, was killed in an accident on Monday.

item.title: Dozens Massacred in Haiti, Officials Say, Heightening Fears of Gangs
item.description: Gangs targeted a key community on the outskirts of the capital, raising fears about the gangs’ next move. The mayor said at least 25 people had been killed, but the U.N. put the death toll at 47.
item.dc:creator: Frances Robles and André Paultre
item.media:description: Dozens of people were killed by armed gangs in Kenscoff, a neighborhood near Port-au-Prince, Haiti, on Sunday into Monday, officials said.

item.title: Canada Fires Back in Trade War Against Trump With Up to 50% Tariffs
item.description: Canada said the higher levies, on items from aluminum foil to dishwashers to fish, would help protect workers, producers and manufacturers harmed by new Trump tariffs.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:description: The U.S. Steel Clairton Coke Plant in Clairton, Pa. Canada has announced it will impose retaliatory tariffs of up to 50 percent on hundreds of American products including steel.

item.title: Christian Convert Who Fled Iran and Was Deported By Trump Finds New Home
item.description: Artemis Ghasemzadeh, who had escaped religious persecution, was deported to Panama under Trump’s immigration crackdown. Now, Canada has given her asylum.
item.dc:creator: Farnaz Fassihi
item.media:credit: Alana Paterson for The New York Times
item.media:description: Artemis Ghasemzadeh at her new home on Denman Island near Vancouver.

item.title: How U.S.-Canada Tariff Negotiations Turned Into an All-Out Trade War
item.description: Detailed accounts of the final hours of the negotiations show that, while the United States offered Canada what it said was the best deal of any country, what Canada had to give up in exchange was seen as unthinkable.
item.dc:creator: Matina Stevis-Gridneff and Ana Swanson
item.category: Office of the United States Trade Representative
item.media:description: Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada speaking about the trade dispute with the United States on Monday at the Davie Shipyard in Levis, Quebec.

item.title: U.S. Tariffs Could Price Canadian Firms Out of U.S. and Threaten Thousands of Jobs
item.description: The 50 percent tariffs President Trump imposed on Canadian exports to the United States will make it impossible for many Canadian companies to continue to sell to the U.S. market, economists say.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:description: Harvested logs in British Columbia in 2023. Canada’s forestry industry may be hit particularly hard by the latest American tariffs.

item.title: Trump Threatens New 50% Tariffs on Cars, Trucks and Steel as U.S.-Canada Trade War Unfolds
item.description: President Trump vowed to increase tariffs on cars, trucks, auto parts and steel to 50 percent starting Jan. 1, as the countries edged toward a full-blown trade war.
item.dc:creator: Ana Swanson and Tony Romm
item.media:description: Trade tensions between the United States and Canada have spiraled over the past few days, after the two sides failed to reach a trade deal and President Trump imposed 50 percent tariffs on $20 billion of the country’s exports on Saturday.

item.title: Can ‘Argentina’s Texas’ Save the Country’s Economy?
item.description: Thousands of Argentines are flocking to a remote stretch of Patagonia, seeking work with only backpacks, tents and the hope that they and their country can turn around their fortunes.
item.dc:creator: Emma Bubola and Sarah Pabst

item.title: How Argentina’s Oil Boom Is Changing Patagonia
item.description: Our correspondent Emma Bubola travels to northwest Patagonia, the epicenter of an oil boom that Argentina hopes will revolutionize its economy.

item.title: Carney Slams U.S.-Canada Trade Proposal and Vows Retaliation
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney gave a powerful speech to Canadians on Saturday morning, hours after ordering negotiators to suspend U.S. trade talks despite President Trump’s punishing tariffs.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:credit: Patrick Doyle/The Canadian Press, via Associated Press
item.media:description: Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada said that he had pulled negotiators out of trade talks with the United States because the Trump administration had “asked too much and offered too little.”
